subject: Television & Streaming
title: I Love Lucy Changed Everything
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: I Love Lucy Changed Everything.

hook.text: In 1951, CBS told Lucille Ball her Cuban husband couldn't be on TV. America wouldn't accept it, they said.

buildup.text: Ball refused to do the show without Desi Arnaz. They formed their own production company to force CBS's hand.

discovery.text: I Love Lucy invented the three-camera setup and filming before a live audience—techniques still used today.

twist.text: Lucy's real pregnancy aired on the show. That episode drew 44 million viewers—more than Eisenhower's inauguration.

climax.text: Ball and Arnaz owned the show's reruns. They became TV's first moguls, proving actors could control their work.

punchline.text: A woman CBS doubted became TV's first mogul.

quiz.question: What production technique did I Love Lucy pioneer?
options: The three-camera setup with a live studio audience
